text:
Jordan (Product): quick pass on the model catalog UI — noticing the quick-filter row feels visually disconnected from the compare grid, esp when badges wrap. wondering if we should treat it as a persistent toolbar or a floating filter chip area.
Priya (Design): I agree, it's visually floating right now. when badges wrap they collide with the compare row actions. proposal: make the quick-filter a fixed height strip with subtle divider and overflow into a 'more filters' pill.
Alex (Eng): making it fixed isn't hard, but need to be careful with vertical real estate on small screens. fixed strip adds ~48px.
Ava (A11y): +1 on clearer separation. also need focus order: keyboard users should hit filters before the compare checkboxes. right now tab order jumps into rows.
Mateo (PM): goal is to surface performance badges and version pin affordance without confusing discoverability. is the 'pin' currently a per-row action or in the compare header?
Priya (Design): pin is per-row today which has been confusing. users expect a global 'pin version' in the compare header or a sticky pin on the left. but we don't want pinning to disappear from row context.
Sam (Research): in recent interviews 4/6 users tried pinning from the header first. per-row pin was treated as a secondary affordance. data suggests header-first pattern.
Jordan (Product): ok so move primary pin to compare header, keep per-row pin as contextual. can we show a tiny persisted state (chip) in the toolbar that lists pinned versions?
Alex (Eng): technically doable: header pin toggles metadata for the compare session, then we annotate rows. might need API change to persist compare session state.
Ava (A11y): for the header pin button, please use aria-pressed and add a visually-hidden label like "Toggle pin mode: press to pin a version for compare". also ensure the pinned-versions chip is announced when it changes.
Priya (Design): noted. sketching two variants: (A) compact header with icon + count, tooltip on hover, keyboard opens a small tray; (B) expanded toolbar with chip list. preference from design: A for density, B for clarity.
Mateo (PM): we should A/B both on desktop for 2 weeks. metrics: pin usage, time-to-compare, and dropped comparisons.
Sam (Research): also watch for misclicks — badges and pins are close. add 8px hit target padding to badges and 10px to pin icon.
Alex (Eng): badge rendering currently uses inline SVGs in the row cell; adding hit padding might shift layout unless we use negative margin click targets. can prototype with CSS like: ``` .badge { padding: 6px 8px; margin: -6px -8px; } ```
Priya (Design): nice. also the badge color contrast needs tweak — some performance badges (light green on white) fail AA at small sizes. Ava, can you confirm?
Ava (A11y): confirmed. the success badge uses #98e6a0 which is too low contrast at 12px font. suggestions: darken to #29a14a or add a 1px stroke. whichever preserves brand.
Jordan (Product): let's pick a color that passes AA and keep the current label text (e.g., "latency: good") shortened to "latency — ok" for space. keep full text in tooltip.
Priya (Design): copy tweak noted. also thinking about filter semantics: users expect filters to be additive but the current quick filter behaves like exclusive mode for model family. we need clearer chip states (active vs toggle).
Sam (Research): most users expect multi-select. the exclusive behavior caused confusion in the test where selecting a family replaced previous selections.
Alex (Eng): existing API supports both modes but the client currently calls exclusive endpoint. easy fix but we'd need to migrate saved filters and update telemetry.
Mateo (PM): prioritize multi-select default, keep an 'only' action in the chip dropdown for power users.
Ava (A11y): for the chip dropdown, ensure role="menu" and role="menuitemcheckbox" for selections. keyboard: space to toggle, Enter to open 'only'.
Jordan (Product): final asks before we implement: 1) move primary pin to header, 2) fixed compact toolbar with overflow pill, 3) multi-select default for families, 4) badge color contrast fix, 5) a11y attributes for toolbar and pin. can we ship a prototype to test next week?
Alex (Eng): can spin up a feature branch and demo by Wed. will need design mocks and exact copy.
Priya (Design): I'll drop two mock variants in Figma by EOD tomorrow and include a11y specs + token values.
Sam (Research): I'll draft a short test script for 6 users focusing on discoverability and pinned compare flows.
deploy-bot: deploy queued — review-app will be available at https://staging.redwood.company/review/3124 in ~30m :rocket:
Jordan (Product): sweet — thanks all. quick nits to include in PR: keyboard focus ring thickness on chips, ensure tooltip delay is 300ms, and add analytics event 'compare_pin_toggled'. :thumbsup:
Priya (Design): noted. will annotate the mocks.
Alex (Eng): creating PR now, linking mocks + a11y checklist. will ping when review-app is live.
Ava (A11y): I'll run axe against the review-app and share results.
Jordan (Product): perfect. if anything blocks the demo ping product. thanks! :clap:
